Join Our Team: Make a Difference in Women's Health and Birth Experiences!

Permanent Part-Time & Fixed-Term Positions Available for:

Birth Suite Midwife

CTG Clinic-Antenatal Assessment Midwife

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Step into a role where you can make a real impact and be part of an exceptional team of skilled Midwives and Obstetricians. At our organization, we are dedicated to creating meaningful and personalized birthing experiences for women in the private sector. You'll be part of a supportive and passionate team committed to delivering the highest standard of care.

This is an exciting opportunity to advance your career with access to leadership roles, education programs, and professional growth. Whether you're looking to grow your expertise or expand your leadership potential, we provide the resources and environment to help you thrive in your midwifery career.

WHY WORK FOR SVPHM:

You will join a high performing team and a workplace with relationships built on mutual trust and respect. We value our staff and offer professional advancement in a respectful, collaborative and learning environment.

Join the St Vincent's Health Australia Group, and work for a truly values based organisation, who operate across VIC, NSW and QLD

Salary packaging available (pay less tax and increase your take home pay!)

Gain access to discounted gym membership through Fitness Passport

Option to join our workplace giving program, Give4Good

A great work life balance with options to purchase additional leave

Receive a staff discount on hospital admissions to any SVHA Private Hospital

 ABOUT ST VINCENTS PRIVATE HOSPITAL MELBOURNE

Our experienced team of clinical professionals, care givers and support staff are equipped to provide the highest level of therapeutic, medical and surgical services. We work together to ensure patient safety, well-being and recovery. We are a not for profit Catholic private hospital which operates across four sites at Fitzroy, East Melbourne, Kew and Werribee.

ABOUT YOU:

As an exceptional Birth Suite Midwife, you are dedicated to providing woman-centred care and utilizing your expertise to create positive, empowering birth experiences.

Your skills and experience include:

Recent hands-on experience in the birth suite.

Proficiency in FSEP and resuscitation skills.

Experience in a CTG Clinic or Antenatal Assessment (preferred).

A deep passion for delivering compassionate, woman-centred care.

If you are committed to making a meaningful impact in women's health and are driven by a passion for excellent care, we would love to hear from you!
 

APPLY NOW!

If this is the role for you, please hit the APPLY button now! Your application must include:

Cover Letter

Resume

We are committed to equal employment opportunity, ethical practices, the principles of cultural diversity and promote a smoke free work environment.

USVD Consultants Pty Ltd (ACN 666 075 065) ABN: 80 993 362 158 is a recruitment company having office at Bella Vista NSW 2153.

Our client APS, Australasian Protective Services (ABN 69 084 470 995) is a Premier Security Company and it is a 100% Australian owned company that provides customisable solutions, including cash in transit, physical manpower presence and technology security solutions to their clients all across Australia. They specialize in tailored electronic security solutions for organizations of all sizes and industries. Electronic security refers to the utilization of advanced technology, such as CCTV cameras, electronic alarm systems, and drone technology, to conduct comprehensive security checks on premises. APS assures safety and security and it is their top priority. 

Due to the business growth and expansion plans, USVD is now looking to recruit  Electronic Equipment Trades Worker(s) in their Technology team on a permanent full-time basis.

Position Title: Electronic Equipment Trades Worker
Location: Laverton North VICTORIA 3026
Reports to: Technology Leader 
No. of position: 02
Offered Salary range: $80,000.00 - $85,000.00 plus Super 

Role purpose:
Electronic Equipment Trades Workers install, maintain and repair electronic equipment and systems such as audio and visual reproduction equipment, home entertainment systems, computers and electronic security systems. As an Electronic Equipment Trades Worker, your duties and responsibilities include:
•	Installing, configuring and commissioning electronic equipment such as CCTV systems, security alarm systems, access control systems, audio-visual equipment, communication systems and electronic control devices.
•	Examining and testing electronic systems and components to diagnose faults using specialised diagnostic tools and electronic testing instruments.
•	Dismantling faulty equipment, identifying defective components and repairing or replacing circuit boards, wiring, connectors, sensors and electronic modules.
•	Reassembling equipment and conducting functional testing to ensure proper performance and compliance with operational specifications.
•	Reading and interpreting circuit diagrams, schematics and technical manuals to perform accurate installation and troubleshooting.
•	Performing routine servicing and preventive maintenance to ensure reliability and reduce equipment failure.
•	Installing and terminating structured cabling and low-voltage wiring systems in accordance with safety regulations.
•	Maintaining documentation including service reports, installation records and compliance documentation.
•	Advising clients and end users on correct system operation, maintenance procedures and safety requirements.
•	Ensuring all work was carried out in compliance with WHS regulations and relevant Australian Standards.

Qualification & Licences:
•	Certificate III in Electronics and Communications or equivalent Tertiary qualifications in Electrical or Electronics engineering.
•	At least 3 years of proven work experience in installing and maintaining electronic equipment or systems. 
•	Strong fault-finding abilities and familiarity with electronic diagnostic tools. 
•	Understanding of WHS requirements, particularly in industrial and construction environments. 
•	Ability to interpret technical drawings, manuals, and specifications.
Skills:
•	Strong organizational and time management skills 
•	Strong problem-solving skills 
•	Excellent attention to detail 
•	Ability to multitask 
•	Process and results driven 
•	Effective communicator, both written and verbal 
•	Team player; collaborative 
•	Resilient, patient and adaptable 
•	Enthusiastic, self-motivated 
•	Proactive 

Additional information: 
•	Ability to work outside of normal business hours on occasion when installing or upgrading components. 
•	Ability to travel interstate, if required.

Job Description
Position Overview:
AI Talent, a pioneer in AI-powered solutions, is looking for a meticulous and experienced Software Tester to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for verifying the quality and performance of our AI applications by creating and executing test plans, identifying defects, and working closely with developers to ensure prompt resolution.
The ideal candidate will bring a solid grasp of software testing methodologies, sharp analytical skills, and a strong commitment to delivering high-quality AI software. Experience with test automation tools is a plus.
Responsibilities:
Collaborate with the development team and project stakeholders to understand software requirements and design comprehensive test plans and test cases for AI software applications.
Perform functional, integration, system, and regression testing to validate the performance, accuracy, and reliability of AI software products.
Identify and document software defects, including clear and detailed reproduction steps, in a bug tracking system. Collaborate with the development team to ensure timely resolution of issues.
Develop and maintain automated test scripts using industry-standard software testing automation tools (e.g., Selenium, Appium, or Robot Framework) to streamline testing processes and improve test efficiency for AI software applications.
Create and maintain test documentation, including test plans, test cases, and test reports, to ensure comprehensive test coverage and facilitate knowledge sharing within the team.
Set up and configure test environments, including hardware, software, and data, to simulate real-world scenarios and ensure accurate testing results.
Continuously evaluate and enhance software testing strategies, methodologies, and tools to improve the overall quality and efficiency of testing processes.
Work closely with the development team, product owners, and other stakeholders to understand requirements, clarify issues, and provide timely feedback on the quality of AI software products.
Collaborate with the QA team to establish and maintain quality standards, best practices, and processes across AI software projects.
Stay up-to-date with the latest trends and advancements in software testing methodologies, AI technologies, and industry best practices.
Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
Must have at least 2 years of proven experience as a Software Tester, with a strong understanding of software testing methodologies and practices.
Experience in testing AI software applications and familiarity with AI concepts and technologies.
Solid knowledge of test management tools, bug tracking systems, and test automation frameworks.
Experience with software testing automation tools such as Selenium, Appium, Robot Framework, or similar.
Proficiency in programming languages commonly used in software testing, such as Python or Java.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and isolate software defects effectively.
Excellent attention to detail and ability to meticulously follow test plans and test cases.
Good communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
Experience with Agile development methodologies is a plus.
Relevant certifications in software testing, such as ISTQB, are desirable.
Permanent Residents (PR) and Australian Citizens are eligible to apply
Job Type: Full-time
Salary: $70,000 to $120,000 per year + super

result.description: Mega HVAC Pty Ltd  Our commitment to quality, innovation, and exceptional customer service has earned us a strong reputation within the industry. With modern manufacturing facilities in Oakleigh, Victoria, and a portfolio that includes major projects such as Footscray Hospital, the University of Melbourne, Chadstone Shopping Centre, and Melbourne Quarter, we continue to support Australia's growing construction sector with reliable, high-quality HVAC solutions.     As our business continues to expand, we are seeking a qualified Welder to join our skilled fabrication team and contribute to the delivery of premium HVAC products.      KEY TASKS    Interpret engineering drawings, fabrication plans, and technical specifications to prepare and weld customised HVAC ductwork and sheet metal components in accordance with project requirements.  Determine appropriate welding techniques, materials, joint configurations, and fabrication sequences to ensure structural integrity, dimensional accuracy, and compliance with manufacturing specifications.  Perform MIG and TIG welding on galvanised steel, stainless steel, and other sheet metal materials used in the manufacture of rectangular, spiral, and oval HVAC duct systems.  Fabricate, assemble, and weld sheet metal ductwork, fittings, supports, frames, and associated HVAC components.  Set up, operate, and maintain welding equipment, hand tools, and fabrication machinery to achieve accurate welds while ensuring safe and efficient production.  Inspect weld preparations, fit-up, alignment, and completed welds to verify compliance with engineering drawings, quality standards, and Australian manufacturing requirements.  Finish welded assemblies by grinding, dressing, deburring, and polishing welds to achieve the required surface quality, dimensional tolerances, and presentation standards.  Collaborate with fabrication and production teams to resolve welding and fabrication issues, ensuring projects are completed efficiently and within scheduled production timelines.  Conduct routine quality inspections and identify defects or non-conformances, carrying out repairs or rework where necessary to maintain MEGA HVAC's high manufacturing standards.  Follow workplace health and safety (WHS) procedures and maintain a clean, organised work area.       REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE    A minimum of 3 years of full-time relevant experience in welding and metal fabrication, preferably within the HVAC or related industry.  At least an AQF Certificate III in Fabrication Trade, Welding, or a relevant trade qualification.  Proficiency in MIG and TIG welding techniques, with the ability to produce accurate, high-quality welds on sheet metal components.  Strong ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, fabrication blueprints, and technical specifications.  Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality workmanship.  Well-developed problem-solving and troubleshooting skills  Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team environment.  Effective communication and interpersonal skills.  Knowledge of relative safety standards and willingness to use protective clothing.  Fluent in English and Vietnamese.       NOTES   Available for face-to-face interview in Oakleigh, VIC 3166.  About Company     MEGA HVAC Pty Ltd is a leading Melbourne-based manufacturer and supplier of high-quality HVAC ductwork solutions, proudly servicing the Australian commercial and industrial sectors for over 28 years. We specialise in the custom fabrication of sheet metal ductwork, including rectangular, spiral, and oval duct systems, delivering precision-engineered solutions tailored to our clients' project requirements. result.description:
Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter
Asia Mideast Insurance and Reinsurance Pty Ltd
Location: North Sydney NSW 2060
Employment Type: Full-time
Position: Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter


About the Business
Asia Mideast Insurance and Reinsurance Pty Ltd, known as AMIR, is an underwriting agency and Lloyd’s of London Coverholder based in North Sydney, New South Wales.
AMIR focuses on underwriting insurance and reinsurance risks, with particular expertise in complex and specialty risks in Australia and overseas. The business actively underwrites risks across Australia, New Zealand, the Middle East, Asia, Africa and the Indian sub-continent.
AMIR has been operating successfully for 28 years and has developed a strong reputation for technical underwriting expertise, profitable underwriting results, responsive broker service and long-standing relationships across international insurance and reinsurance markets.


About the Role
AMIR is seeking a full time Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter to join its North Sydney office.
The successful candidate will be responsible for underwriting property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance risks across Australian and international markets. The role requires advanced technical underwriting capability, strong commercial judgement, experience in high risk property, power and construction exposures, and the ability to work closely with insurance and reinsurance brokers, cedants, capacity providers and internal stakeholders.
This is a senior technical underwriting role which will involve risk assessment, pricing, broker liaison, portfolio development, risk mitigation planning, review of survey and loss information, and training of junior underwriting staff.


Key Duties and Responsibilities
The Senior Property, Power & Construction Underwriter will be responsible for:
•	Underwriting property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance risks in accordance with AMIR’s underwriting authorities, binder requirements and internal procedures. 
•	Assessing complex property, power and construction risks, including exposure, construction type, occupancy, location, loss history, survey findings, policy terms, risk mitigation measures and underwriting suitability. 
•	Reviewing and analysing risk survey reports, engineering information, loss records, policy wordings, slips, endorsements and supporting underwriting documentation. 
•	Preparing underwriting recommendations, pricing, terms, conditions and coverage positions for property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance risks. 
•	Developing technical underwriting plans to manage high-risk exposures across property, power and construction classes of business. 
•	Applying risk modelling techniques and relevant risk assessment tools to evaluate exposure, probable loss and underwriting acceptability. 
•	Reviewing applicable sanctions, territorial issues and compliance considerations relevant to international insurance and reinsurance risks. 
•	Liaising with insurance and reinsurance brokers in Australia and overseas to obtain underwriting information, clarify risk details and negotiate appropriate terms. 
•	Developing and maintaining strong relationships with insurance and reinsurance brokers to support quality business submissions and long term portfolio development. 
•	Attending relevant industry seminars, conferences and market meetings in Australia and overseas. 
•	Undertaking business travel as required to meet insurance and reinsurance brokers, promote AMIR’s underwriting capabilities and increase appropriate business opportunities. 
•	Liaising with loss adjusters and relevant professional advisers in relation to major property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance losses. 
•	Applying Lloyd’s of London risk codes, reporting expectations and underwriting requirements where relevant. 
•	Supporting portfolio monitoring, renewal reviews, underwriting performance analysis and internal reporting. 
•	Training and mentoring an Assistant Underwriter appointed from the Australian market in underwriting processes, broker liaison, risk assessment and business development matters. 


Skills and Experience Required
The successful applicant will be expected to have:
•	Minimum 10 years’ underwriting experience in property, power and construction insurance and/or reinsurance. 
•	Minimum 7 years’ experience underwriting property, power and construction risks in the Middle East. 
•	Demonstrated experience in underwriting high-risk property, power and construction exposures. 
•	Strong familiarity with risk mitigation measures for complex insurance and reinsurance exposures. 
•	Experience using risk modelling techniques and relevant tools for property, power and construction risk assessment. 
•	Strong relationships with insurance and reinsurance brokers across international markets, excluding USA and Canada. 
•	Familiarity with sanctions regimes applicable to international insurance and reinsurance risks. 
•	Ability to review risk survey reports and identify relevant underwriting information required for proper risk assessment. 
•	Experience dealing with international loss adjusting firms in relation to large property, power and construction insurance and reinsurance losses. 
•	Familiarity with Lloyd’s of London risk codes, binder requirements and underwriting standards. 
•	Ability to train junior underwriting staff in technical underwriting, broker liaison and business development matters. 
•	Academic engineering knowledge or engineering-related qualifications to support technical risk assessment. 
•	Proven track record of profitable underwriting results. 
•	Strong written and verbal communication skills. 
•	High level attention to detail and ability to work accurately within underwriting guidelines, binder requirements and compliance obligations. 
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant underwriting, reporting, risk assessment or risk modelling systems. 


Qualifications
Relevant qualifications in insurance, reinsurance, engineering, risk management, business, finance or a related field will be highly regarded.
Professional Insurance qualification minimum Diploma in Insurance from the Chartered Insurance Institute in UK, or Australian equivalent. 


How to Apply
Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant property, power and construction underwriting experience.
Applications should be sent to: adel@amir.com.au
